overview.title: The project owns a tree of work
overview.explanation: Ownership arrows point from owning Group to owned child. The Step block summarizes three distinct leaf objects, not one shared instance. The inheritance arrow describes the Group type, whereas the ownership links describe this example tree. Each child query returns a subtotal upward; ownership does not mean call direction.

focus.title: Accept a completed owned subtree
focus.start: // Take a finished list of children.
focus.what: Construction transfers a list of exclusive owners and rejects a missing child.
focus.where: This is the point where a new Group takes responsibility for its subtree.
focus.why: Validating once prevents every later query from having to handle null children.
focus.invariant: All accepted entries own real Work objects and remain inside the group.
focus.risk: Manually manufacturing duplicate owners can still violate unique_ptr rules.

focus.title: Return a checked subtotal
focus.what: Each group computes a fresh sum from its child queries.
focus.where: This block is the recursive part of Group::minutes.
focus.why: One uniform query handles both leaf durations and nested subtotals.
focus.invariant: total remains between zero and ten thousand throughout successful execution.
focus.risk: Adding before checking or accepting a negative child result breaks the bound.
